text:
Ana (Design): quick design pass on the new prompt-sets test-runner screen — can we do a fast round of bikeshedding on the diff vs side-by-side layout?
Mike (PM): sure — main concern from PM is that reviewers can spot regressions at a glance and approve small fixes quickly. :eyes:
Sophie (Eng): side-by-side is clearer for token-level diffs but takes a lot of vertical space, esp for long responses. compact stacked diffs with inline highlights might be better for scannability.
Ana (Design): agreed. what about a collapsed summary row for each test that expands into the full diff? keeps list density high.
Ravi (a11y): note on accessibility — if we use expand/collapse, ensure the control is keyboard focusable and aria-expanded toggles. add offscreen labels for screen readers like "Expand regression details for <test name>".
Mike (PM): good call. also copy: current CTA says `Approve` — ambiguous. is it approving the suite, the specific test change, or the whole rollout?
Ana (Design): we should change to `Approve change` for single-test approvals and `Approve suite changes` for bulk. display a confirmation toast that lists approved test IDs.
Sophie (Eng): implementation note: we can wire a bulk-approve endpoint that takes an array of test ids. backend can return per-test result, then show a small table in the toast if any failed.
design-bot: deploy-preview available at https://staging.redwood.ai/ux/prompt-tests — branch: feature/test-diffs-ui
Ana (Design): +1 to showing a small diff summary pill at the right edge with color-coded severity (info/warn/error). colors need to meet contrast.
Ravi (a11y): color contrast: the orange severity color is failing 4.5:1 on light backgrounds. propose swapping to #D65A00 or adding a 2px outline for focus states. also ensure the severity icons have aria-hidden and textual label next to them.
Mike (PM): UX question — when a regression is detected, do we show an inline revert/rollback action or require going to the model rollout page? I'd prefer inline quick-actions for small fixes.
Sophie (Eng): inline revert is fine but should be gated behind a confirmation modal with a short reason field. make sure audit logs capture who clicked it.
Ana (Design): wording for the confirmation modal: header: `Confirm quick rollback`, body: `This will revert the prompt change for this test. Add a brief reason (optional).` primary CTA: `Revert change`, secondary: `Cancel`. any copy nits?
Ravi (a11y): modal needs focus trap, initial focus on the reason textarea, and role=dialog with aria-labelledby. also ensure Escape closes and `Revert change` is reachable via Enter when focused.
Mike (PM): good. one more: when reviewers skim many diffs, the scorecard compact mode should hide code blocks by default and show a short 2-line excerpt with a "Show full output" link. speed matters.
Ana (Design): mockup attached in the preview branch — uses a chevron to expand each output and a lightweight diff-highlighter. can we get engineering lift estimate? @Sophie
Sophie (Eng): rough: 3-4 days to wire the expand/collapse + bulk API + a11y tweaks. more if we add animated transitions.
Ana (Design): perfect. last tiny nit — microcopy for the regression badge: current `Regressed` feels harsh. suggestion: `Quality drop` or `Behavior change`?
Mike (PM): `Behavior change` is clearer to non-technical reviewers. let's use that.
Ravi (a11y): also add a tooltip with the exact metric delta, and ensure the tooltip is keyboard accessible (`aria-describedby`).
Ana (Design): thanks all — I'll update the staging mock with the copy changes and post a short test plan. if no objections I'll move this to the next design sprint. :sparkles:
Mike (PM): no objections from me.
Sophie (Eng): sounds good.
Ravi (a11y): 👍
Ana (Design): tagging this for design review on Tuesday 10am PT.
